title: Lambda / Cloud Run / Azure Functions connector instance config (loams.flow/v1)
description: One function invocation sink's settings, read by the native protocols family (`loams_connector_protocols::functions`, CN2 Task 21): one invocation per event, the answer a reply event on `reply_topic` (R-CN2-3, R21.8). `aws.*`, `id_token` and `function_key` hold secret **names** (D189), exactly the manifest's `secrets`.

provider.description: `lambda` (`iam`: SigV4), `cloud_run` (`sa`: an ID token) or `azure_functions` (`aad`: a function key).

function.description: Lambda: the function name or ARN.

endpoint.description: Lambda: the API endpoint; `https://lambda.<region>.amazonaws.com` when omitted.

aws.description: Lambda: AWS credentials by secret name, and the signing scope.

access_key_id.description: The access key id. The **name** of a secret in the namespace's store (D189), resolved when the connector connects; never the value.

secret_access_key.description: The secret access key. The **name** of a secret in the namespace's store (D189), resolved when the connector connects; never the value.

session_token.description: A session token, for temporary credentials. The **name** of a secret in the namespace's store (D189), resolved when the connector connects; never the value.

url.description: Cloud Run and Azure Functions: the function's URL.

id_token.description: Cloud Run: an ID token whose audience is the service, minted and rotated by the secret store. The **name** of a secret in the namespace's store (D189), resolved when the connector connects; never the value.

function_key.description: Azure Functions: the function key (`x-functions-key`). The **name** of a secret in the namespace's store (D189), resolved when the connector connects; never the value.

body.description: A body template (`{{/field}}`, `{{data}}`, `{{subject}}`, `{{id}}`); the event's data as is when omitted.

function_error.description: What a function error becomes: `poison` (the DLQ) or `reply` (a reply `{function_error, payload}`).

reply_topic.description: Where replies go: one reply event per input, `io.loams.dev.flow.lambda-cloud-run-azure-functions.reply.v1` with id `<input id>/reply`, keeping the input's subject and carrying `loamsinreplyto`/`loamsinreplytosource` (OR-19, R21.6). Without it no replies are sent.
